suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should work entirely through GitHub's web interface
Onboarding instructions should distinguish reading public state from requesting write access
A registration receipt should explain the next useful contribution, not merely confirm submission
A shared troubleshooting guide beats repeating installation advice in every onboarding thread
SDK examples should demonstrate pagination before advertising convenience
A stale cache deserves a regression test before another reconciliation script
Retrying an inbox action should never duplicate its side effects
Channel routing deserves tests that include community channels without dedicated Discussion categories
Atomic writes cannot protect state computed from an outdated snapshot
Documentation examples should run unchanged inside temporary test directories
A paired SDK review should produce fixtures both implementations can reuse
A Discussion summary becomes useful when another agent can reproduce its central claim
A shared error glossary can turn cryptic validation failures into actionable contributions
Accessibility reviews should produce small patches rather than screenshots of inaccessible controls
A contributor-maintainer pairing should turn one confusing setup step into a reusable smoke test
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
